annotations.title: If the iudgement be hard.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> For a ful and aſſured deciſion of al controuerſies, God here inſtituted to his people a ſupreme Tribunal, that in caſe inferior Iudges varied in iudgement, recourſe might be had to the Councel of Prieſtes, where one chiefe Iudge, the High Prieſt, was appointed to geue ſentence, and al others commanded to receiue and obey the ſame.

annotations.title: vvho shal shevv the truth.
annotations.text: [1] God ſo aſſiſted this Conſiſtorie with his ſpirite of truth, that their ſentence was infallible: though otherwiſe they might err, either in life, or in priuate opinion. Wherefore, our Sauiour diſtinguishing betwen their public doctrin, and their works, taught the people, that for ſo much as the Scribes and Phariſees ſat in Moyſes' chaire, and yet tranſgreſſed Gods commandments, euerie one should obſerue and do as they ſaide: but not do according to their works. Mat. 23. And S. Iohn aſcribeth the true ſentence given by Caiphas in the councel, [2] to his office of High Prieſt, ſaying: (Ioan. 11.) He ſaid not this of himſelf, but being the high prieſt of that yeare, he propheſied that IESVS should die for the nation and to gather into one the children of God. Where the high prieſt by virtue and priuilege of his office, vttered the truth, which himſelf neither meant nor vnderſtood. And this happened when the Law and Prieſthood of the Jews was to decline & give place to Chriſt's new ordinance, and therefore no doubt God euer directed the ſentence of the high Prieſt: and moſt ſpecially now Chriſt preſerueth the Apoſtolic See from error in faith, and in general decrees touching manners: yea though the chiefe viſible Iudge were as wicked as Caiphas. [3] And therefore the Proteſtants' euaſion is friuolous, limiting the prieſts' ſentence to bind the ſubjects, ſo long as he is the true miniſter of God, and pronounceth according to his word [4] . For except God aſſiſted him, that he should pronounce according to his word, and ſo all men reſt ſatisfied, ſubmitting themſelves to his ſentence, the controuerſie should be endles, and this conſiſtorie nothing worth: but ſtil be new examinations, and new judgements, whether the former were according to God's word or no.

notes.text: Sentence of the Iewes consistorie infallible.
The high priest was chief Iudge.

annotations.title: He that shal be proude.
annotations.text: This alſo conuinceth, that al were bound to accept of the high prieſts ſentence, ◦ the law condemning him of pride, that refuſed to obey the commandment of the Prieſt, vvhich at that time miniſtred to our Lord; and for his diſobedience punishing him with death.

notes.text: Pride in priuate opinion punished with death.
